domain_label: AI-Designed D2C Knitwear Contribution-Margin-After-CAC P&L and Viability Test
purpose: A session-bounded method for the owner of an AI-designed D2C knitwear brand (Ludhiana-sourced, California/Turlock-sold, 3-article line A1 cotton-blend core / A2 fine-acrylic value / A3 merino-lambswool premium) to test real viability the way the SCOPE_GLOSSARY rule #8 demands: contribution margin after CAC, not gross margin, decides D2C survival. It sets the per-article MSRP ladder, stacks the four costs below gross margin (payment, returns reserve, ship-to-customer, blended CAC plus platform/app fees), recomputes contribution-after-CAC per order and the AOV needed, applies the LTV:CAC>3 gate, and produces a blunt go/no-go verdict in which the 80-86 percent gross margin is a vanity trap, A2 at 55 dollars loses money on the first order at realistic CAC, A1 at 75 dollars only works at CAC under ~38 dollars with repeat, and only A3 at 145 dollars plus 2-unit bundles (AOV ~120-150) reliably pays for a customer and clears the gate.
assumptions: no live ad account, returns log, or repeat-purchase data exists for a brand that does not yet operate; every CAC, returns, conversion, and repeat number is a labeled estimate keyed to apparel-D2C benchmarks, not measured cohorts
landed COGS is inherited from the T9 landed-cost work (A1 ~11, A2 ~11, A3 ~20 dollars as band-centre illustrations) and is treated as COGS-to-stock, not re-derived here

the operating model is the post-de-minimis default: bulk Importer of Record into a California/Turlock 3PL then domestic ship, so duty is paid once at import and is already inside landed COGS, not a per-order line
duty rates are facts carried from T9: cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5 percent, wool 6110.11 ~16 percent, acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32 percent; the discredited ~7 percent cotton figure is never used
the entire CAC/returns/repeat/contribution spine is single-analyst (Analyst-B) and adversarially flagged by Analyst-C; benchmarks are governing yet softest, resolvable only by a live test
MSRP ladder is the controllable design choice; the viability verdict treats AOV ~120-150 and blended CAC under ~35 dollars as the two levers that decide whether the line closes
exclusions: landed-cost and duty derivation (owned by the T9 landed-cost analyst; consumed here as a COGS input, not recomputed)
yarn, machine, manufacturing-economics, QC, and finishing cost build-up upstream of landed COGS
the macro/decision-brain go/no-go synthesis across all specialists (owned by T10) beyond handing it this P&L verdict
brand creative, AI-design generation, and channel content production mechanics (owned by the T7 brand and T8 design specialists) beyond naming CAC as their economic constraint
tax, entity, and accounting treatment beyond the per-order contribution identity and the fixed monthly nut estimate
the working-capital cash-cycle model as a full treasury forecast (named here as the dominant non-P&L kill-risk, not modeled per dollar)

competency_questions.question: For each article in the line, what is the MSRP and where does it sit on the pricing ladder that bounds every contribution calculation downstream?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MSRP_LADDER states A1 at 75, A2 at 55, A3 at 145 dollars (and a 2-unit bundle at ~120-150 AOV), ties each to its landed COGS band, and frames the ladder as the controllable design lever the verdict acts on

competency_questions.question: Why is the 80-86 percent gross margin a vanity trap rather than the viability number, and what does it exclude?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GROSS_MARGIN_TRAP shows gross margin over landed COGS at 80-86 percent for all three articles and names the four below-gross costs it ignores, asserting per glossary rule #8 that contribution-after-CAC, not gross margin, decides survival

competency_questions.question: What are the four costs that sit below gross margin, and which one governs the whole verdict?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BELOW_GROSS_STACK enumerates payment ~3 percent, returns reserve 15-30 percent, ship-to-customer ~7-8 dollars, blended CAC 45-70 dollars plus platform/app fees, and names CAC as the governing term because it is the same order of magnitude as the entire gross margin

competency_questions.question: What is the realistic blended CAC for a new no-name apparel brand, and is the under-35-dollar bar achievable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAC_BENCHMARK gives the 45-70 dollar new-cohort blended band (worst-quartile ~187, best ~42, plus the ~35 percent CPM penalty) and states the under-35-dollar bar is achievable only as a built organic/community/affiliate engine, not a launch dial

competency_questions.question: How is contribution-after-CAC computed per order, and does the formula recompute cleanly from MSRP, landed COGS, the cost stack, returns, and CAC?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTRIBUTION_AFTER_CAC states the identity contribution = (MSRP - landed COGS - payment - ship - returns load) - CAC, recomputes it, and shows pre-CAC contribution per article (A2 ~22.74, A1 ~37.76, A3 ~82.92) before subtracting CAC

competency_questions.question: At realistic CAC, which articles make or lose money on the first order?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: A2_ACRYLIC_PNL shows A2 underwater at any realistic CAC (-2 to -47), A1_COTTON_PNL shows A1 marginal and CAC-fragile (positive only under ~38 with repeat), A3_MERINO_PNL shows A3 positive even at 70 dollars CAC

competency_questions.question: What is the CAC ceiling per article, the maximum CAC before the first order loses money?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAC_CEILING recomputes the per-article ceiling (A2 ~23, A1 ~38, A3 ~83, 2-unit bundle ~69) and contrasts it against the realistic 45-70 dollar CAC so A2 fails, A1 is fails-to-marginal, A3 and bundles pass

competency_questions.question: How does the LTV:CAC>3 gate change the picture once realistic repeat is applied, and does it recompute?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LTV_CAC_GATE recomputes allowable CAC = (pre-CAC contribution x repeats)/3, shows that at real repeat ~1.2x even A3's clearing CAC falls to ~33, and concludes only A3 and bundles clear 3:1 and only with organic-cheap acquisition

competency_questions.question: What AOV makes the line close, and why is bundling the decisive pricing move?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BUNDLE_AOV shows a 2-unit ~130 AOV amortises one CAC and one ship over a bigger basket, survives CAC to ~69, and states the required AOV is ~120-150 (one premium unit or a 2-piece bundle), never a single 55-dollar sweater

competency_questions.question: What is the break-even order volume, and on which two inputs is it a knife-edge?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BREAKEVEN_VOLUME recomputes orders/mo = fixed nut / contribution-per-order, gives ~75-150 orders/mo at a lean 1,500-3,000 nut with ~20-dollar contribution, and shows it doubles to 300+ if CAC drifts to 70 or contribution falls to 10

competency_questions.question: Why can a per-order-profitable brand still die, and what is the unmodelled killer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WORKING_CAPITAL_TRAP names the dye-lot MOQ plus ocean lead time plus returns-settlement cash-out cycle, flags that it overlaps the slow organic-CAC ramp, and states per-order viability is necessary but not sufficient

competency_questions.question: How are CAC, returns, and repeat numbers stated honestly without faking precision a non-existent brand cannot have?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCHMARK_HONESTY tags every CAC/returns/repeat/conversion claim [FACT], [ESTIMATE] (method+basis+confidence, literal word estimate), or [UNKNOWN], flags the spine as single-analyst un-cross-examined, and names the live test as the only thing that hardens it

competency_questions.question: What legal exposure does the AI-designed naming/creative strategy carry, and why is it a hard gate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEGAL_PUBLICITY flags right-of-publicity (Cal. Civ. Code 3344/3344.1, living and deceased) and Lanham 43(a) false-endorsement exposure for any athlete/celebrity name or likeness, notes AI-design does not launder a likeness, and requires mark clearance before printing or any creator post

competency_questions.question: What is the blunt go/no-go verdict, on what conditions does it flip, and on what cadence is it re-tested?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VIABILITY_VERDICT states GO only premium-led/bundle-driven/A2-in-baskets at blended CAC under ~35 funded through the cash cycle, NO-GO as a value-led cold-paid-social brand; VIABILITY_REVIEW_LOOP sets the re-test triggers (live CAC, surcharge, returns, repeat) that re-run the P&L

glossary.definition: Price minus all variable costs (landed COGS plus payment fees plus ship-to-customer plus returns load) and then minus the customer acquisition cost; per SCOPE_GLOSSARY rule #8 this, not gross margin, is the metric that decides D2C survival, and on it the line's stated value article (A2) is the biggest loss-maker.

Gross margin over landed COGS runs 80-86 percent on all three articles and looks fantastic, but it ignores payment, returns, shipping, and CAC; treating it as the viability number is the central error this KB exists to correct.

Marketing/sales spend divided by new customers across all channels; benchmarked at 45-70 dollars for a new no-name apparel cohort (worst-quartile ~187, best ~42, with a ~35 percent CPM penalty for no brand history), it is the governing term because it is the same order of magnitude as the entire gross margin.

The maximum CAC at which the first single order still breaks even, computed as pre-CAC contribution per article; estimated A2 ~23, A1 ~38, A3 ~83, 2-unit bundle ~69 dollars, the bar the realistic 45-70 dollar CAC is measured against.

The standard D2C survival test that lifetime contribution must exceed three times acquisition cost; allowable CAC = (pre-CAC contribution x repeat orders)/3, and at real apparel repeat ~1.2x even A3's clearing CAC falls to ~33 dollars, folding every article back into needing organic-cheap acquisition.

Average order value; because CAC and outbound shipping are charged per order not per unit, bundling amortises one CAC and one ship over a bigger basket, so lifting AOV to ~120-150 (a 2-unit bundle or one A3) is the single pricing move that makes the line close.

A provision for the fit-driven return rate on a sight-unseen fine-gauge sweater, estimated 15-30 percent of orders (central 22-25 percent, plausibly 30 percent) plus ~10-12 dollars reverse logistics and ~20 percent dead-stock; it is a contribution drain that hits the high-value A3 hardest in absolute dollars.

The four costs gross margin ignores: payment processing ~2.9 percent + 0.30 dollars, returns reserve, ship-to-customer ~7-8 dollars, and blended CAC, plus platform/app subscription and transaction fees; subtracting them converts a healthy gross margin into the honest per-order contribution.

Cash tied up between paying for dye-lot-MOQ bulk inventory and being paid by customers; ocean lead time plus sell-through plus returns settlement strand cash for months, and this overlaps the slow organic-CAC ramp so a per-order-profitable brand can still die in the cash gap around month seven.

The acquisition mode (founder short-form content plus commission-only affiliate/TikTok-Shop plus owned email, paid social as minority filler) that delivers the under-35-dollar blended CAC the verdict needs; it is a stock the owner builds over quarters, not a flow bought at launch, and its single point of failure is whether the owner can produce organic content that performs.

nodes.definition: Pin the MSRP ladder that bounds every contribution calculation downstream: A1 cotton-blend core at 75 dollars on landed COGS ~11, A2 fine-acrylic value at 55 dollars on landed COGS ~11, A3 merino-lambswool premium at 145 dollars on landed COGS ~20, plus a deliberate 2-unit bundle engineered to an AOV ~120-150. The ladder is the controllable design choice the whole verdict acts on; price, not fibre, decides which article can pay for a customer, so the spread between the 55-dollar value floor and the 145-dollar premium ceiling is the first lever set before any cost is stacked.

included: per-article MSRP and its landed-COGS pairing
the bundle price point feeding AOV

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an article MSRP, the bundle price, or the landed-COGS pairing changes

pros.claim: Fixing the MSRP ladder first gives every contribution figure a fixed numerator and exposes the price-not-fibre logic before costs muddy it
pros.example: setting A3 at 145 dollars makes its later survival at 70-dollar CAC traceable to price headroom, not to the merino itself

cons.claim: A fixed ladder can anchor the analysis to MSRPs the market may not bear, hiding a price-elasticity problem the contribution math then inherits

failure_modes: importing a single-unit price as if the line is sold one sweater at a time when bundles are the real unit
treating MSRP as fixed when promotion and markdown move realised price below it

edge_cases.description: The line launches A2-led on cold paid social and bleeds on every first order
edge_cases.trigger: a value-led launch sells the 55-dollar A2 single at a 45-70 dollar CAC
edge_cases.mitigation: invert the line to premium-led A3 plus bundles, A2 only as a bundle-filler, and never lead with the value single

edge_cases.description: Repeat is assumed at 2.5x when real apparel repeat is ~1.2x, hiding an LTV failure
edge_cases.trigger: the LTV gate is run with the generous T9 repeat instead of the measured category rate
edge_cases.mitigation: re-run the gate at ~1.2x repeat, exposing that even A3's clearing CAC falls to ~33 and needs organic-cheap acquisition

edge_cases.description: First-cohort returns come in at 30 percent rather than the modelled 22 percent
edge_cases.trigger: a fit-sensitive fine sweater returns at the high end of the apparel band
edge_cases.mitigation: model 25-30 percent returns, which hit A3 hardest in absolute dollars, and re-derive every contribution figure

edge_cases.description: The brand is per-order profitable but runs out of cash in month seven
edge_cases.trigger: dye-lot-MOQ bulk inventory plus the slow organic ramp strand cash simultaneously
edge_cases.mitigation: fund the bulk-inventory and organic-ramp cash gap before committing, and treat per-order profit as necessary-not-sufficient

edge_cases.description: Blended CAC drifts from 45 to 70 dollars and break-even doubles
edge_cases.trigger: organic underperforms and the owner leans on paid, driving CAC up 20-30 percent YoY
edge_cases.mitigation: hold paid as minority filler, keep the organic engine as the spine, and re-run break-even at the drifted CAC

edge_cases.description: An athlete or celebrity name/likeness is used on a sweater or in a creator post without a license
edge_cases.trigger: an athlete/event/meme naming hook ships before mark and likeness clearance
edge_cases.mitigation: clear marks and likenesses before any print or creator post; AI-design does not launder a recognizable likeness

edge_cases.description: The India surcharge returns to 25-50 percent at the first bulk-PO window
edge_cases.trigger: Section 122 sunsets ~Jul 2026 and a 301-driven tariff lands on the launch window
edge_cases.mitigation: stress-test landed COGS at a 25-50 percent surcharge, which compresses the A3 carrying margin, and re-confirm the rate per PO

edge_cases.description: A single 55-dollar A2 single is sold standalone instead of inside a bundle
edge_cases.trigger: the storefront offers the value article as a standalone hero SKU
edge_cases.mitigation: configure A2 only as a bundle-filler at an effective higher unit price so its CAC and ship amortise across a >=120 AOV basket

edge_cases.description: A band-centre contribution figure is quoted downstream as a measured cost
edge_cases.trigger: an [ESTIMATE] dollar figure loses its tag and is treated as precise
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] tag and confidence on every figure and flag the single-analyst spine

edge_cases.description: The owner commits a bulk PO before any organic-traction signal exists
edge_cases.trigger: inventory is bought before the 60-90-day organic probe returns a result
edge_cases.mitigation: sequence the 0-500 dollar organic probe and the 1-2k paid test before any bulk PO so demand is signalled before cash is stranded

edge_cases.description: Free returns shipping is offered and the reverse leg is omitted from the cost stack
edge_cases.trigger: a generous return policy adds reverse shipping on the 25-30 percent that come back
edge_cases.mitigation: load the reverse leg onto the returns reserve and the shipping line so contribution is not over-stated

workflow.description: Fix A1 75, A2 55, A3 145 dollars and the ~120-150 bundle AOV against landed COGS
workflow.gate: each article MSRP and the bundle AOV is paired to its landed-COGS band

workflow.description: Read A1 ~11, A2 ~11, A3 ~20 dollars with duty embedded as a band-centre input
workflow.gate: landed COGS is stated per article with duty embedded and flagged as an inherited band

workflow.description: Show 80-86 percent gross and subordinate it to contribution-after-CAC per rule #8
workflow.gate: gross margin is stated and explicitly subordinated to contribution-after-CAC

workflow.description: Segment payment, returns, ship, CAC plus platform fees and name CAC as governing
workflow.gate: the four cost lines are segmented and CAC is named the governing term

workflow.description: State the 45-70 dollar band and frame the under-35 organic engine
workflow.gate: the CAC band and the under-35 built-organic-engine framing exist

workflow.description: Evaluate the contribution identity to per-article pre- and post-CAC figures
workflow.gate: the identity recomputes pre-CAC contribution A2 ~22.74, A1 ~37.76, A3 ~82.92

workflow.action: Resolve the per-article and bundle P&Ls
workflow.description: Show A2 underwater, A1 marginal, A3 robust, and the bundle as the AOV lever
workflow.gate: each article's post-CAC sign and the bundle AOV result are stated

workflow.action: Apply the CAC ceiling and LTV:CAC>3 gate
workflow.description: Recompute ceilings and the gate at real repeat ~1.2x against the realistic CAC
workflow.gate: the gate recomputes at ~1.2x repeat so even A3 needs organic-cheap CAC

workflow.action: Recompute break-even and name the cash trap
workflow.description: Derive ~75-150 orders/mo and flag the working-capital/organic-ramp overlap
workflow.gate: break-even orders/mo is recomputed and the cash trap is named as necessary-not-sufficient

workflow.action: Apply the honesty and legal gates
workflow.description: Tag every CAC/returns/repeat claim and flag right-of-publicity/Lanham exposure
workflow.gate: every soft claim is tagged and the legal hard gate is flagged
the verdict states the GO conditions and the value-led NO-GO with the operating model

workflow.action: Set the review loop and de-risking probe sequence
workflow.description: Sequence the organic probe plus paid test before any bulk PO and set re-test triggers
workflow.gate: the probe/test sequence precedes the bulk PO and the material-change triggers route back to the contribution identity and gate

priority_rationale: The MSRP ladder, inherited landed COGS, and the gross-margin trap come first because every contribution figure depends on a fixed numerator, an inherited denominator, and the rule that gross margin is not the viability number; the below-gross stack and the governing CAC benchmark supply the subtrahends; the contribution-after-CAC formula and the per-article and bundle P&Ls evaluate the identity; the CAC ceiling, LTV:CAC>3 gate, break-even volume, and working-capital trap test survival against real repeat and cash timing; honesty and legal gates keep the numbers and creative honest; and the consolidated verdict plus its live-test review loop compose everything into a conditional go/no-go that the review loop routes back to the contribution identity and gate.

dominance_rules.rule: Contribution-after-CAC dominates gross margin as the viability number
dominance_rules.rationale: per SCOPE_GLOSSARY rule #8 gross margin ignores the four below-gross costs, so an 80-86 percent gross figure proves nothing about survival
dominance_rules.trigger: any judgment of viability framed on gross margin
dominance_rules.action: subordinate gross margin to contribution-after-CAC and decide on the post-CAC figure

dominance_rules.rule: The LTV:CAC>3 gate at real repeat dominates the lenient first-order ceiling
dominance_rules.rationale: passing the first-order CAC ceiling is necessary-not-sufficient; real repeat ~1.2x pulls even A3's clearing CAC to ~33
dominance_rules.trigger: an article is declared viable on the first-order ceiling alone
dominance_rules.action: re-run the LTV gate at real repeat and require organic-cheap CAC to clear 3:1

dominance_rules.rationale: a per-order-profitable brand still dies in the bulk-inventory plus organic-ramp cash gap around month seven
dominance_rules.trigger: viability claimed on per-order contribution without a cash plan
dominance_rules.action: require funding of the working-capital and organic-ramp gap before any GO

dominance_rules.rule: Premium-led/bundle pricing dominates the value-single instinct
dominance_rules.rationale: a standalone 55-dollar A2 single loses 2-47 dollars per order at realistic CAC; only AOV >=120 pays for a customer
dominance_rules.trigger: a plan to lead with or sell A2 as a standalone hero
dominance_rules.action: invert the line to A3 plus bundles and use A2 only as a bundle-filler

dominance_rules.rule: Honesty labeling dominates any contribution or CAC figure
dominance_rules.rationale: the spine is single-analyst and un-cross-examined, so an untagged number fakes precision a non-existent brand cannot have
dominance_rules.trigger: any CAC/returns/repeat/contribution figure stated without a tag
dominance_rules.action: carry [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] with method and confidence and flag the single-source spine

dominance_rules.rule: Right-of-publicity/Lanham clearance dominates a creative likeness hook
dominance_rules.rationale: a recognizable athlete/celebrity likeness creates profits-disgorgement liability that dwarfs any CAC saving, and AI-design does not launder it
dominance_rules.trigger: a naming or creator hook uses a real name or likeness
dominance_rules.action: clear marks and likenesses before any print or creator post

dominance_rules.rule: The organic-traction probe dominates the inventory commitment
dominance_rules.rationale: the verdict rests on a cheap-CAC engine the owner has not proven, so the demand signal must precede the cash-stranding bulk PO
dominance_rules.trigger: a bulk PO is proposed before the organic probe returns a result
dominance_rules.action: run the 0-500 dollar 60-90-day organic probe and the paid test before committing inventory

dominance_rules.rule: The verdict's direction dominates but is held open by the review loop
dominance_rules.rationale: the GO/NO-GO direction is robust while its softest inputs are one live test from hardening or collapsing
dominance_rules.trigger: the verdict is treated as final rather than conditional
dominance_rules.action: keep the direction but bind it to flip-conditions and the live-test review loop

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the MSRP ladder and inherited landed COGS before computing any contribution
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-deriving every article P&L after a late price or COGS change

anti_rework_rules.rule: Subordinate gross margin to contribution-after-CAC at first statement
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a viability case on a gross-margin number that later collapses post-CAC

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the LTV gate at real repeat ~1.2x, not the generous 2.5x, from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: declaring articles viable on a repeat assumption the gate then reverses

anti_rework_rules.rule: Model returns at 25-30 percent for a fit-sensitive fine sweater, not 22 percent
anti_rework_rules.prevents: over-stating every contribution figure and re-doing the P&L when real returns land high

anti_rework_rules.rule: Treat per-order profit as necessary-not-sufficient and price the cash gap before GO
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a per-order-profitable verdict that ignores the month-seven cash-out and reverses

anti_rework_rules.rule: Configure A2 as a bundle-filler, never a standalone hero, before storefront build
anti_rework_rules.prevents: shipping a money-losing 55-dollar single SKU that must be repriced into bundles

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every CAC/returns/repeat/contribution figure estimate-or-fact when first written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a band-centre estimate being quoted downstream as a measured per-order cost

anti_rework_rules.rule: Sequence the organic-traction probe before any bulk-inventory PO
anti_rework_rules.prevents: stranding working capital in inventory before the cheap-CAC engine is signalled to work

iteration_protocol.trigger: a live blended-CAC reading arrives from a paid or organic test
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the contribution identity, CAC ceilings, and the LTV gate at the measured CAC

iteration_protocol.trigger: a first-cohort returns or repeat rate is measured
iteration_protocol.action: re-parameterise returns and repeat and re-derive every article P&L and the gate

iteration_protocol.trigger: the line plan re-prices an article or changes the bundle/AOV
iteration_protocol.action: re-set the MSRP ladder and recompute contribution, ceilings, and break-even

iteration_protocol.trigger: the India surcharge or duty moves at the bulk-PO window
iteration_protocol.action: re-read landed COGS and re-stress the A3 carrying margin in the verdict

iteration_protocol.trigger: the organic-traction probe returns a breakout or flat result
iteration_protocol.action: flip the verdict toward GO or NO-GO and re-run the review loop

iteration_protocol.trigger: a naming or creator hook introduces a real name or likeness
iteration_protocol.action: re-clear the legal gate before any print or post

iteration_protocol.trigger: the fixed monthly nut or the financing of the cash gap changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-run break-even volume and the working-capital-trap funding precondition
